name: uv projects, workspaces, and lock discipline
short_definition: Astral uv as the sole greenfield Python package/project manager: pyproject projects, uv.lock, PEP 735 dependency groups, workspaces, sync/run/CI --locked workflows, replacing pip/poetry/pip-tools/pyenv stacks.
scope_in: uv init/add/remove/sync/lock/run; uv.lock semantics; [project] dependencies vs [dependency-groups]; workspaces and tool.uv.sources; requires-python interaction; GitHub Actions setup-uv; basic publish/build awareness; monorepo layouts next to Next/Axum.
scope_out: Deep supply-chain malware policy (py-uv-audit-supply-chain); full Docker multi-stage recipes (py-docker-deploy); legacy setup.py packaging; conda/pixi environments; private index auth vault design beyond noting index-url config.
defaults: One tool: uv for installers, venvs, lock, run, and Python versions. Greenfield: uv init → uv add deps → commit pyproject.toml + uv.lock + .python-version. Use PEP 735 [dependency-groups] for dev/lint/test (dev group synced by default); use [project.optional-dependencies] extras only for published optional features. Workspaces when multiple Python packages share one lock in a monorepo; otherwise single project or path sources. CI always: uv sync --locked (and --all-groups or explicit groups as needed). Never Poetry+pip-tools for new services.
decision_gates: Use uv project mode: any new app/lib service. Use workspaces: multiple interdependent Python packages in one repo needing one lock. Use path sources without workspace: conflicting requires-python or separate venvs needed. Use extras (optional-dependencies): installable features for consumers of a library. Use dependency-groups: local dev/test/lint only (not shipped as extras). Avoid uv only as pip drop-in long-term — prefer project interface. Keep poetry.lock only during migration; delete when uv.lock is authoritative.
do_dont: DO: commit uv.lock; use uv add / uv remove so lock stays consistent; uv sync --locked in CI; declare workspace members with globs and workspace = true sources; put pytest/ruff/basedpyright in dependency-groups. DO NOT: hand-edit uv.lock; use requirements.txt as primary for apps (export only when ops demand); mix poetry and uv as dual sources of truth; forget --locked in CI; put secret index credentials in pyproject; use --no-dev in prod images intentionally when you need zero dev tools.
code_skeleton:
# Create
# uv init svc-api --package
# uv python pin 3.13
# uv add fastapi 'uvicorn[standard]' pydantic
# uv add --dev pytest pytest-asyncio ruff basedpyright

# pyproject.toml (single project)
[project]
name = "svc-api"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
  "fastapi>=0.115",
  "uvicorn[standard]>=0.32",
  "pydantic>=2.10",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
  "pytest>=8.3",
  "pytest-asyncio>=0.24",
  "ruff>=0.15",
  "basedpyright>=1.39",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["uv_build>=0.11.28,<0.12"]
build-backend = "uv_build"

# Workspace root excerpt
# [tool.uv.workspace]
# members = ["packages/*"]
# [tool.uv.sources]
# shared-lib = { workspace = true }
failure_modes: CI without --locked installs newer transitive deps than prod. Lock not committed → non-reproducible deploys. Workspace member omitted from members globs → resolution surprises. Conflicting dependency groups still resolve together (uv resolves all groups for one lock) — incompatible pins fail lock. Dev group bloated into production image because sync omitted --no-dev. Editable workspace imports leak undeclared deps across members (Python has no isolation).
anti_patterns: Agents must not: generate Poetry [tool.poetry] greenfield layouts; write pip freeze workflows as primary; invent dual lockfiles; use requirements.in + pip-tools for new apps; skip uv.lock in .gitignore; call pip install inside Docker without uv; add deps only to pyproject without locking.
tools: Primary: uv (CLI), astral-sh/setup-uv for GHA. Alternatives (legacy only): pip+venv, poetry, pdm, hatch — migrate off for greenfield. Build backend: uv_build or hatchling as project needs. Companion: ruff, basedpyright installed via dependency-groups.
versions_as_of: as_of 2026-07-13 — uv 0.11.x on PyPI (e.g. 0.11.28); local Homebrew sample 0.11.23. PEP 735 dependency-groups supported; universal uv.lock. setup-uv GitHub Action in active  v8 line per docs examples. Pin exact uv version in CI for supply-chain stability.

deprecation_watch: Greenfield avoid: Poetry as primary; Pipenv; pip-tools as app workflow; manually maintained requirements.txt without lock generation story; setup.py without pyproject; pyenv-virtualenv chains when uv python suffices; committing .venv.
ts_boundary: In a monorepo with Next.js, keep Python under services/ or packages/python/* with its own uv.lock — do not share node_modules. Orchestrate CI jobs separately (pnpm vs uv). Boundary contracts remain HTTP/OpenAPI; package managers never cross languages.
rust_boundary: Rust stays on Cargo workspaces; uv workspaces are Python-only. A hybrid repo may host crates/ and python/ packages/* side by side. Call Rust via HTTP/gRPC or PyO3 wheels published/path-sourced — do not expect uv to build Rust except via custom build scripts.
supabase_boundary: Add supabase and/or asyncpg/sqlalchemy via uv add; lock pins transitive HTTP/Postgres clients. Prefer service-role keys only in server env, not in pyproject. Migrations: keep Supabase SQL or Alembic in-repo; uv does not replace migration tooling.
boundary_contracts: uv.lock + pyproject.toml are the install contract for Python services; OpenAPI is the cross-language API contract; env for secrets; optional uv export requirements.txt only for external systems that cannot run uv. MCP tool servers packaged as uv projects with --no-dev deploy sync.
decision_matrix_row: Python packaging/lock/run → uv always. TS packages → pnpm. Rust → cargo. Do not introduce Poetry for new Python in this stack.
threats: Malicious or typosquat packages resolved into lock; compromised index; lockfile PR that quietly bumps vulnerable transitive; credentials in uv.toml committed; installing with --no-verify or disabled hashes in hostile networks.
mitigations: Commit and review uv.lock diffs; CI --locked; prefer default hash checking; pin setup-uv action by commit SHA; use private index config via env/secret not git; run audit skill (uv audit / OSV) in separate item; least-privilege tokens for publish.
agent_codegen_policy: MUST generate: pyproject.toml with [project], requires-python, dependencies; [dependency-groups] dev for tools; instruct uv lock/sync; commit uv.lock. MUST NOT generate: poetry.lock, Pipfile, setup.py-only projects for greenfield; pip install -r without uv path; secrets in config files.
tests_required: CI sync --locked succeeds on clean runner; uv run pytest; optional uv lock --check (or equivalent freshness check) on PRs; workspace builds each member package import smoke test.
ci_gates: setup-uv with version pin; uv sync --locked --all-groups (or explicit); fail on lock drift; cache uv store per action defaults; no poetry install steps in greenfield workflows.
skill_scan_signals: Positive: uv.lock committed; [dependency-groups]; astral-sh/setup-uv; uv sync --locked. Negative: poetry.lock without migration note; requirements.txt sole source; unpinned pip install in Dockerfile; missing lock; both poetry and uv without documented dual-run period.
skill_module_bullets: Greenfield Python packaging is uv-only: init/add/lock/sync/run — not Poetry/pip-tools.
Always commit uv.lock; CI must uv sync --locked.
Use PEP 735 [dependency-groups] for dev/test/lint; reserve optional-dependencies for published extras.
Workspaces: one lock, members globs, tool.uv.sources workspace = true for in-repo packages.
Prod images: uv sync --locked --no-dev; never copy host .venv.
Pin uv version in CI (setup-uv commit SHA); review lockfile diffs like package-lock.

conflicts_noted: Some teams still prefer hatchling vs uv_build as build-backend — either fine; uv docs examples use uv_build. Workspaces force a single requires-python intersection — conflicting member floors need path deps instead. uv resolves all dependency groups together for the lock, which surprises users expecting fully isolated group resolution.
